title: Sun: SDO HMI continuum map (Stellarium sun.webp)
owner: NASA Solar Dynamics Observatory, HMI (data); map by Ruslan Kabatsayev for Stellarium (commit 2aa98a95, 2025-09-15)
source: Stellarium textures/sun.webp at commit 9910a2f0 (8192x4096 WebP, sha256 a1fc496b...)
licence_quote: Stellarium CREDITS.md section 4.3o: "The Sun map was created by Ruslan Kabatsayev from the images taken by SDO HMI. The map is under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International license."
adaptations: Averaged 8x8 in linear light to 1024x512; the intensity is kept and Stellarium's uniform warm tint is replaced by the TSIS-1 solar colour (sRGB [255, 244, 241]); JPEG quality 85. The adapted map data/tex/sun.jpg is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0.
accuracy: A generic texture, per its commit message: sunspots from HMI images of 2025-08-07 to 08-31, the rest spotless data of 2019-12-15, each image used only in the central 60 % of the disc; limb darkening removed; no Carrington registration, so longitudes carry no meaning. The source is monochrome HMI 617 nm continuum data; the colour is the measured TSIS-1 colour, not HMI's.

title: Earth at night: Earth's City Lights (DMSP-OLS), KDE Marble copy
owner: Marc Imhoff (NASA GSFC), Christopher Elvidge (NOAA NGDC), Craig Mayhew and Robert Simmon (NASA GSFC)
source: KDE/marble data/maps/earth/citylights/citylights.jpg at commit 600d542e (2700x1350, sha256 c79ca569...)
licence: Public domain (as labelled in KDE Marble's citylights.dgml)
licence_quote: citylights.dgml @600d542e: <license short="NOAA NGDC, NASA / Public Domain">Source: Marc Imhoff of NASA GSFC; Christopher Elvidge of NOAA NGDC; Craig Mayhew and Robert Simmon, NASA GSFC, License: Public Domain</license>
adaptations: Box-filtered 2700x1350 -> 2048x1024 (PIL BOX), JPEG quality 85. The dgml gives no bounds; the left edge -180 is proved by registering the map's own land/ocean base against the Blue Marble (best shift 0, not mirrored) and by the positions of Tokyo, New York, Moscow, Cairo, Paris and Sao Paulo (verify_textures_sky.py).
accuracy: DMSP satellite data of about 2000, composited over a dark land and ocean base (not a pure emission layer).

title: Moon: LROC WAC Hapke-normalised albedo map (Stellarium moon_4k.jpg)
owner: NASA LRO / LROC team, Arizona State University (data); map by Ruslan Kabatsayev for Stellarium (commit ef231c69, 2026-03-13)
source: Stellarium textures/moon_4k.jpg at commit 9910a2f0 (4096x2048, sha256 ad4435c7...)
licence_quote: Stellarium CREDITS.md section 4.2: "Moon albedo map was generated by Ruslan Kabatsayev from Hapke-normalized LROC WAC data for visible-light wavelengths, plus empirically-normalized data for 643 nm to cover the polar areas. The spectra were converted to linear sRGB, then scaled up by a factor of 4, and then the sRGB inverse transfer function was applied. The polar areas, being monochromatic in the original data set, were colored using a fit to the equatorial sectors. After this the image was color-balanced to yield the grayish look of the texture instead of the natural beige color of the lunar surface. The map is under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International license."
adaptations: Averaged 2x2 to 2048x1024, JPEG quality 85. The adapted map data/tex/moon.jpg is shared under CC BY-SA 4.0.
accuracy: Albedo with shading removed (suits the app's own lighting). Disclosed processing that is not measurement: brightness x4, polar colour fitted from the equatorial sectors, and colour balanced to grey instead of the natural beige. Longitude convention proved by Tycho, Mare Humorum and the maria/highlands asymmetry.

source: USGS Astrogeology public bucket asc-pds-services, mosaic/Mars_Viking_ClrMosaic_global_925m.tif (797,888,177 bytes, sha256 5b3c6bea36cec0ec..., md5 a0e0bbf33ecb0ff65ece9cfa8e08813e = the USGS sidecar), with its ISIS label Mars_Viking_ClrMosaic_global_925m.lbl
adaptations: About 1000 red- and violet-filter images, Minnaert-normalised and haze-corrected (FGDC abstract). Area-averaged (every source pixel counted once, nodata excluded) to 2048x1024, east-positive, left edge -180 deg (ISIS label: PositiveEast, planetocentric, CenterLongitude 0, -180..180; GeoTIFF central_meridian 0); JPEG quality 85.

title: Jupiter: Cassini ISS global colour map PIA07782 (December 2000)
owner: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute (Cassini Imaging Science Subsystem); USGS Astrogeology copy
source: USGS asc-pds-services wms_basemaps/Jupiter/Jupiter/originals/jupiter_rgb_cyl_www.jpg (4096x2048, sha256 0c6fa8e9...), with the annotated original jupiter_from_cassini.tif for the longitude labels
licence: JPL Image Use Policy: any purpose with a credit line. The Space Science Institute is a non-NASA co-credit; the policy notes that such third-party material may carry restrictions on commercial use.
licence_quote: USGS mapfile maps/jupiter/jupiter_simp_cyl.map: "Image credit by NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute."; JPL Image Use Policy (CelestiaContent LICENSES/JPL-image.txt): "may be used for any purpose without prior permission, subject to the special cases noted below" ... "to use a credit line in connection with images" ... "Some image and video materials on JPL public web sites are owned by organizations other than JPL or NASA. These owners have agreed to make their images and video available for journalistic, educational and personal uses, but restrictions are placed on commercial uses."
adaptations: Averaged 2x2 to 2048x1024, JPEG quality 85. Not flipped: the annotated original labels its x axis 180, 150, ... 0, 330, ... 180, i.e. west longitude decreasing to the right, so east longitude increases to the right; left edge 180 W (-180 E). The web copy is the same picture (correlation 0.999 at zero shift, 0.85 mirrored). The web copy's world file puts the left edge at longitude 0 instead, 180 deg from the annotation; the annotation is followed.
accuracy: A snapshot of 11-12 December 2000 from 36 images in two filters (451 and 750 nm) combined to near-natural colour; the poles were poorly observed, and the source map is one flat colour [169, 173, 156] over the south polar region (4.3 % of the pixels): not imaged, not terrain. Features drift in longitude, so the Great Red Spot (about 21 S in this map) will not match any other date; the file does not state the longitude system.

title: Pluto: New Horizons LORRI/MVIC global mosaic 300 m (July 2017)
owner: NASA, Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, Southwest Research Institute, Lunar and Planetary Institute (FGDC originators); distributed by USGS Astrogeology
source: USGS Astrogeology public bucket asc-pds-services, mosaic/Pluto_NewHorizons_Global_Mosaic_300m_Jul2017_8bit.tif (309,806,463 bytes, sha256 592b7fb0f88cafa0..., md5 3a137d75e3a1a325f3de037a27563ffa = the USGS sidecar), with its ISIS label Pluto_NewHorizons_Global_Mosaic_300m_Jul2017_8bit.lbl
licence: No licence stated: FGDC access constraint "None", use constraint "Please cite authors"; a NASA mission product distributed by USGS. Credited as asked.
adaptations: Panchromatic LORRI and MVIC images of the 2015 flyby. Area-averaged (every source pixel counted once, nodata excluded) to 1024x512, east-positive, left edge 0 deg (ISIS label: PositiveEast, CenterLongitude 180, 0..360 (left edge 0 E); GeoTIFF central_meridian 180); JPEG quality 85. 31.8 % of the pixels had no data: flat DN 109 (mean of the imaged pixels) where New Horizons saw nothing (mostly south of ~30 S, in polar night during the 2015 flyby): not imaged, not terrain.
accuracy: Its label puts the map's centre at 180 E (0..360); Sputnik Planitia checked at 175 E, 20 N. Resolution is very uneven (sharp on the encounter hemisphere). The flat grey area is where New Horizons saw nothing (southern polar night); it is not terrain. Longitudes are in the frame the mosaic was made in (nh_targets_v001 / pck00010 per its ISIS label).

title: Disk colours: Karkoschka (1998) albedo spectra of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Titan, 300-1050 nm
owner: Erich Karkoschka; ESO spectrophotometry of 1995-07-06 to 07-10; NASA Planetary Data System
source: PDS3 product 1995LOW.TAB and its label, carried verbatim in OrbitalCommons/starfield crates/surfaces/data/planet-spectra at commit 5cbc6620 (sha256 d8071e07... / 6fa49ffa...)
licence: PDS archive data (the label states no licence); the carrying repository is MIT-licensed
licence_quote: 1995LOW.LBL: DATA_SET_ID = "ESO-J/S/N/U-SPECTROPHOTOMETER-4-V2.0"; Low-resolution data from: Methane, Ammonia, and Temperature Measurements of the Jovian Planets and Titan from CCD-Spectrophotometry by Erich Karkoschka (ICARUS 1998).; starfield LICENSE: "MIT License Copyright (c) 2024 Matthew Goodman"
adaptations: Each spectrum x TSIS-1 sunlight integrated against the CIE 1931 2-degree colour-matching functions (as tabulated in colour-science 0.4.6, BSD-3-Clause), 1 nm steps 360-830 nm, Y = 1 for a white reflector, Bradford-adapted from the Sun's white to D65, IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB: Jupiter [193, 193, 178], Saturn [197, 185, 156], Uranus [157, 195, 202], Neptune [137, 183, 202], Titan [145, 126, 95].
accuracy: Disk-averaged colours of July 1995 (Uranus's colour changes with its seasons); Jupiter, Saturn and Titan are full-disk albedo at 5.7-6.8 deg phase, Uranus and Neptune geometric albedo. An equal-energy illuminant instead of TSIS-1 changes them by at most 3 of 255.

owner: NASA TSIS-1 / LASP (Coddington et al. 2023); 1 nm resampling by OrbitalCommons/starfield
source: crates/surfaces/data/solar-spectrum/tsis1_hsrs_v2_1nm.csv in OrbitalCommons/starfield at commit 5cbc6620 (sha256 c27ca614...); LASP LISIRD itself is not reachable from the build network
licence: No licence in the file; the carrying repository is MIT-licensed
licence_quote: File header: "TSIS-1 Hybrid Solar Reference Spectrum (HSRS) version 2, resampled to 1 nm box means." / "Source: Coddington et al. (2023), Earth and Space Science, doi:10.1029/2022EA002637"; starfield LICENSE: "MIT License Copyright (c) 2024 Matthew Goodman"
adaptations: Colour of sunlight above the atmosphere: CIE xy [0.3216, 0.3321], about 6022 K (McCamy), sRGB [255, 244, 241] with the brightest channel at 255; used for the Sun's disc and to tint the Sun map. Also the illuminant for the planets' disk colours.
accuracy: Solar-minimum spectrum, 0.3 % archive uncertainty over 460-2365 nm (file header).

title: Sky backdrop: Gaia DR3 source counts (STScI/MAST HATS point map)
owner: European Space Agency (ESA), Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC): Gaia Data Release 3. HATS catalogue by the LSST Interdisciplinary Network for Collaboration and Computing, hosted by STScI/MAST on AWS Open Data.
source: point_map.fits (S3 bucket stpubdata, gaia/gaia_dr3/public/hats/gaia, versionId ap2bO438Iyoss8CsAujiN7K4GnPVyjVV, sha256 3bec7fbb3140c3bb...), and the source_id and _healpix_29 columns of partitions Norder=4/Npix=115 and Norder=3/Npix=29 (read by range requests at pinned versionIds, content pinned by sha256)
licence: CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO (non-commercial). ESA's Gaia licence page could not be read from the build network; a web-search summary of cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia-users/license gives CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO, and CelestiaContent's Gaia-derived data/stars.dat.license states the same. The AWS Open Data Registry entry only says "Attribution required".
licence_quote: AWS Open Data Registry datasets/mast-gaia-dr3.yaml @00eb3872: "License: Attribution required." and "This [HATS](https://hats.readthedocs.io/en/stable)-formatted catalog was produced by the LSST Interdisciplinary Network for Collaboration and Computing."; CelestiaContent data/stars.dat.license @eab93932: "SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-CC-BY-NC-3.0-IGO"; acknowledgement (as quoted in AT-HYG ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md): "This work has made use of data from the European Space Agency (ESA) mission Gaia (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/gaia), processed by the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC, https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia/dpac/consortium). Funding for the DPAC has been provided by national institutions, in particular the institutions participating in the Gaia Multilateral Agreement."
adaptations: Two partitions of the MAST copy repeat rows (the same source_id up to 3 times): Norder=3/Npix=29 1,616,125 rows, 1,418,703 distinct; Norder=4/Npix=115 1,368,113 rows, 543,481 distinct. Their 257 HEALPix pixels were recounted from distinct source_id, giving 1,811,709,793 sources. Counts per square degree interpolated bilinearly onto a 2048x1024 ICRS equirectangular grid (RA increasing to the right), asinh stretch (black 2,500, soft 20,000, white 1,200,000 per deg^2, recorded in data/sky/sky.json), grayscale JPEG quality 85. Shared under the same terms (non-commercial).
accuracy: Star counts, not surface brightness: the bulge and the Magellanic Clouds are bright, bright stars do not stand out, and dust shows as holes. NSIDE 256 (0.23 deg pixels). The shipped 8-bit pixels invert (sky.json stretch) to the densities to a median 1.7 %, 99th percentile 11 % (verify_textures_sky.py). A global duplicate check of all 2,016 partitions was out of reach (8 GB of source_id); ten more suspicious partitions were checked clean by the research verifier.
